text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The accuracy decline observed when storing more than 40 items is caused by increased cross‑fact interference, which can be mitigated by introducing periodic consolidation (summary/compression) as described in the accumulation‑vs‑compression paper, thereby stabilizing QA performance beyond the 40‑item threshold.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["562412ff","72ccf918"],"tags":["interference","consolidation","accuracy_drop","memory_management"]},{"statement":"The superiority of the rewrite‑based memory over naive append stems from implicit virtual paging: rewrite limits token growth similarly to MemGPT’s paging between in‑context and external memory, explaining why the append baseline exceeds the token budget while rewrite stays within limits.","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["ad2ef3b4","a962f389"],"tags":["memory_rewrite","append_vs_rewrite","virtual_paging","token_budget"]}]}
